title: Best Pregnancy Pillows UK
short: Seven maternity support pillows tested by pregnant testers, compared on shape, cooling, support and whether they double as nursing pillows.
intro: A pregnancy pillow supports the bump, hips and back to help you sleep comfortably and safely, especially once side-sleeping becomes important. This guide is based on Mumsnet's tested roundup (updated March 2026), with a panel of pregnant testers using each pillow at various stages of pregnancy, alongside advice from senior midwife Marie Louise (The Modern Midwife) and midwife Pip Davies. Prices shown are those quoted by Mumsnet and change often, so check before buying.

products.name: Adjustable Pregnancy Pillow
products.best_for: Anyone who wants fully customisable, long-lasting support and doesn't mind the price
products.key_spec: Full-length body pillow, 150 x 20cm, silicone clamps for adjustable shaping, machine-washable cotton/spandex cover
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Tina found it comfortable, tactile and soothing, using it most nights to support her hips and growing bump, plus for lower back support while sitting up and elevating her legs. Designed by Norwegian chiropractors, its ergonomic microbead filling and silicone clamps let you adjust the shape individually, and she found herself missing this customisable comfort when trying a U-shaped alternative. It's pricey and can be tricky to keep clean, though the cover is machine washable.

specs.Price guide: Check retailer for current price (sometimes discounted around £135)

pros: Really soft
Filling relieves pressure in key areas
Adjustable design offers positioning versatility

products.name: Cooling Body Pillow
products.best_for: Pregnant women who overheat at night and want hip and spinal support
products.key_spec: Full body, gentle C-shape, 120 x 35cm, Stratos cool-touch cotton cover, recycled PET fibre filling
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Zoe loved the cool-touch technology, saying it really helped cool her down getting into bed and when swapping sides during a hot stage of pregnancy. She rated it highly for support and said hip pain she'd had in this and her previous pregnancy completely vanished when using it. It can also be used as a nursing pillow after birth. It's expensive and may not be long enough for taller women.
pros: Cool-touch cover helps with night sweats
Filling made from recycled PET bottle fibres
Provides hip and spinal alignment support
Can be used as a nursing pillow too
cons: May not be long enough for taller women

products.name: U-Shaped Pregnancy Pillow
products.best_for: All-round support for bump, back, legs and neck at an affordable price
products.key_spec: Full body pillow, U-shape, choice of cooling or warming velvet cover
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Amber found it reduced how often she woke up lying on her back. The U-shape curves around the body to support hips, back, neck and bump, and it doesn't cost the earth at around £60. Mumsnet notes it can also help with sciatica, fibromyalgia, back pain and reflux beyond pregnancy. Like most full-body pillows it takes up a lot of space in bed.
pros: Supports bump, back, legs and neck all in one
Keeps its shape and can be moulded
Choice of cooling or warming fabric cover
cons: Takes up a lot of space in bed

products.name: Pregnancy Pillow
products.best_for: Buyers who want one pillow that adapts from pregnancy through to feeding and baby support
products.key_spec: Modular C-shape (140cm) that separates into a smaller nursing pillow and a baby support pillow, washable covers
products.summary: A Mumsnet forum favourite, described by one user as really good for stopping her rolling onto her back and helping lower back and hip pain, with the bonus that it converts for use until baby is around a year old. Its real selling point is the modular design: take it apart and reassemble it as a large C-shaped pregnancy pillow, a smaller breastfeeding pillow, or a compact baby support pillow. It's quite the investment at full price and large in its full form.

specs.Type: Whole body C-shape, adapts to 2 other sizes

pros: Multi-purpose: adapts to a nursing pillow and baby support
Variety of chic, washable cover designs
Offers good, firm support

products.name: Nursing Pillow
products.best_for: Compact, budget-friendly support that carries on being useful after birth
products.key_spec: Adjustable U-shaped, 32 x 50 x 18cm, 100% cotton, tie-around design
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Bethan, testing it as a nursing pillow, gave it five stars and loved the tie-around design that let her find and hold the best position easily, noting the polyfibre filling offers good support for both pregnancy and feeding. It's technically more of a breastfeeding pillow, so its compact size means it can only target one area at a time during pregnancy, but it's cheaper than most and easily transportable.
pros: Cheaper than a lot of options
Can be adapted for bump or leg support during pregnancy
Compact and easily transportable
cons: Doesn't offer as much support as more bespoke pregnancy pillows

products.name: SnuzCurve Pregnancy Pillow
products.best_for: Women who want a pillow that actively guides posture rather than just cushions
products.key_spec: Full body pillow, 135 x 30 x 25cm, built-in KneeBlade design, designed with physiotherapists and midwives
products.summary: Designed by a panel including physiotherapists, chiropractors and midwives to keep you in the safest, most comfortable position, with a KneeBlade section that guides your legs into the optimum sleeping position and takes pressure off back and joints. Mumsnet's tester Tara said it's worth it for posture and recommends starting early to get used to it. One Mumsnetter with SPD in a previous pregnancy wondered if early use had helped this time. A parent-tester found it not as comfy as other maternity pillows, and it can take some getting used to.
pros: Guides you into the correct sleep position
Creates a neutral spine posture to reduce back pain
Built-in KneeBlade design, plus a free sleep support video series
cons: Not as comfy as other maternity pillows, according to one tester
Can take some getting used to

products.name: Pregnancy Support and Feeding Pillow
products.best_for: Back sleepers who need to be discouraged from rolling onto their back
products.key_spec: Full body pillow with integrated back support, 55 x 50 x 19cm
products.summary: Mumsnet's editor Tina rated the support it gave her bump and hips at night during the second and third trimesters, and found the lower back support excellent, saying it feels nice and cosy nestled between the two sides once adjusted. Its unique shape fits around you to discourage rolling onto your back, which can be dangerous after the first trimester. It isn't as individually adaptable as the bbhugme, but at around £38 it's far cheaper. The shape may not suit taller women, and some users find it too firm and flat.

specs.Type: Full body pillow with integrated back

pros: Integrated back support
Can be used after pregnancy for feeding
Much cheaper than premium alternatives
cons: Shape may not suit taller women
Some users find it too firm and flat
products.search: Dreamgenii Pregnancy Support and Feeding Pillow

guide.a: A C-shape like the Simba or BellaMoon supports the bump and back on one side and is easier to move around in bed. A U-shape like the Momcozy wraps fully around you for support on both sides but takes up more space, which Mumsnet notes as its main downside.

guide.q: Do I need a pregnancy pillow to stop me sleeping on my back?
guide.a: It's recommended to avoid sleeping flat on your back after the first trimester. The Dreamgenii's integrated back support and the SnuzCurve's KneeBlade are both designed specifically to discourage rolling onto your back and guide a safer sleep position.

guide.q: Will it still be useful after the baby arrives?
guide.a: Several of these convert to nursing pillows: the BellaMoon splits into a breastfeeding pillow and baby support pillow, the Simba and Momcozy can double as nursing pillows, and the Hippychick and Dreamgenii are designed with feeding in mind from the start.

guide.q: Is a premium pillow worth the price?
guide.a: The bbhugme is the most expensive here but its adjustable design won over Mumsnet's tester, who missed its customisable comfort when trying cheaper alternatives. If budget is tighter, the Dreamgenii or Hippychick offer solid support for a fraction of the price.
